analysis.title: FX Daily Snapshot: Hawkish BoJ update provides support for JPY (30 October 2026)
key_insights: The BoJ held its policy rate at 1.25% with one dissent. Hajime Takata voted to hike, arguing underlying inflation has reached the price stability target and the Bank needs to speed up tightening toward the neutral rate. MUFG calls the overall communication hawkish.

The BoJ unanimously decided to speed up equity ETF sales from January 2027. The annual pace rises from JPY330 billion to JPY860 billion (book value). That lifts sales from 0.05% to 0.1% of stock market trading value and cuts the time to sell all holdings from about 112 years to 43 years. MUFG says it is unclear why the pace was raised so suddenly.

The BoJ said for the first time that the negative correlation between JPY and equities has strengthened. It also said underlying inflation is now consistent with the 2% target across four indicator categories.

The BoJ raised its median core inflation projections (ex fresh food and energy) to 2.7% for FY2027 and 2.3% for FY2028. It sees price risks skewed to the upside and growth risks as balanced. It flagged the risk that inflation expectations rise and underlying inflation overshoots 2%.

MUFG expects another quarterly BoJ hike in December. Governor Ueda said the Bank will weigh a hike at every meeting including the next, and that the policy rate is still below neutral. Markets price 20bps of hikes for December, which MUFG says explains the muted USD/JPY reaction.
USD/JPY fell to a low of 157.12 after the BoJ decision, then rose back to 157.70, leaving it largely unchanged on the day.

MUFG thinks the ECB could have hiked on Thursday if not for the tightening in financial conditions Lagarde acknowledged. A hike was discussed. Fed Chair Warsh also acknowledged tighter financial conditions, which may have contributed to the Fed holding rates.

The ECB and the Fed are each priced at about 80% to hike in December. MUFG sees the equity market channel, not the rates channel, as where the danger lies after another bad day for AI stocks. Alphabet closed down 12.6%, the largest market cap value decline on record, on weaker AI-affected advertising revenue.

US Q3 GDP grew 3.4% Q/Q SAAR after 2.2% in Q2 and beat expectations. Personal consumption grew 3.8%, the same as Q2. MUFG attributes the consumption to AI-related equity wealth gains for wealthier households, since real after-tax income grew only 1.0% YoY. UST yields fell despite the strong print.

Net exports subtracted 3.3ppts from Q3 GDP growth as goods imports rose 26.4% after gains of 15.3% in Q2 and 17.2% in Q1. The US trade deficit with South Korea, Taiwan and Mexico is surging on AI and tech demand.

MUFG says rising equity volatility from doubts over AI valuations could weigh on the dollar, because US economic strength depends heavily on AI. The dollar's strength this month is a euro story, with the dollar weaker versus all other G10 currencies.
earnings_insights: Alphabet closed down 12.6% on 29 October, the worst market cap value decline on record. MUFG attributes the drop to weaker advertising revenues impacted by AI.

risk_factors: Further tightening of financial conditions through an equity sell-off driven by AI valuation doubts could change ECB and Fed hike pricing.
The US dollar is vulnerable to a turn in AI momentum because the US economy depends heavily on AI-related investment and wealth effects.
The BoJ sees a risk that medium- to long-term inflation expectations rise and underlying inflation overshoots 2%, as firms shift toward raising wages and prices.
The BoJ's faster ETF sales add an unexplained equity supply source from January 2027.
The widening US trade deficit from AI and tech imports is a drag on GDP, with net exports subtracting 3.3ppts in Q3.
vol_and_positioning: MUFG notes rising equity volatility tied to doubts over AI valuations, with Alphabet's 12.6% drop on 29 October the largest market cap loss on record.
Markets price 20bps of BoJ hikes for December. MUFG says this is why USD/JPY barely moved after the hawkish meeting.
The ECB and the Fed are each priced at about 80% to hike in December.

tension_points.bull_case: The US economy is strong, with Q3 GDP at 3.4% Q/Q SAAR and consumption growing 3.8%, and the dollar has gained this month against the euro.
tension_points.bear_case: US strength depends heavily on AI-driven investment and equity wealth effects, with real after-tax income growth of only 1.0% YoY. A turn in AI momentum leaves the dollar vulnerable, and the dollar is already weaker versus all other G10 currencies this month.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growing equity volatility from doubts over AI valuations, as seen in Alphabet's 12.6% one-day drop, would undermine the dollar-strength case.

theme_stances.key_argument: The BoJ's updated forecasts and Ueda's comments point to continued quarterly tightening, with a hike likely in December.
The US economy is highly dependent on AI, so rising equity volatility over AI valuations could weigh on the dollar.
